scope: Norway medical discovery — Norwegian University of Science and Technology Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences

verifiedFacts.claim: NTNU's professional Medicine study is Norwegian-taught, has an application deadline of 15 April through Samordna Opptak, and requires Norwegian-language qualifications or a Scandinavian mother tongue.

NTNU describes its Medicine professional study as six years with early patient contact and integrated preclinical, paraclinical and clinical education from the first year; all students start the first two years in Trondheim.
NTNU's 2026–27 tuition table lists a medicine-category annual fee of NOK 528,650, while noting applicable exemptions must be assessed separately.
NOKUT lists NTNU as a university with authority to establish programmes at all levels under the institutional category.

holdReasons: The programme's Norwegian-language requirement prevents presenting it as a generally accessible international English-medium route.
The public tuition category requires current route-specific confirmation of applicability and exemption conditions for Medicine applicants.
A complete programme-specific recognition, clinical-placement, accommodation and international support packet was not completed.
